title: Uncertainty in Kessler cascade modeling
bottleneck: Whether low Earth orbit is already past the tipping point into a self-sustaining collision cascade depends on models fed by uncertain inputs: the true sub-10-cm population, future launch rates, disposal-rule compliance, and breakup physics. Different models give different answers, and the uncertainty is large enough that policymakers cannot tell whether aggressive removal is urgent or merely prudent. The 25-year disposal guideline itself rests on 1990s modeling now considered insufficient for congested shells.
why_it_blocks: Policy — removal funding, disposal rules, launch licensing — needs a risk number; if the models cannot agree, regulation oscillates between complacency and overreaction, and neither stabilizes the environment.
current_state: ESA's annual space environment report tracks the trends; interagency studies continue. No consensus model commands policy.
